parts:

"D3" only available using maximum likelihood estimation. Changed test to "D2".
If test = 'scaled.shifted' (estimator = 'WLSMV' or 'MLMV'), model comparison is only available by (re)setting test = 'D2' and pool.robust = TRUE.
Control more options by passing arguments to lavTestLRT() via the '...' argument.

Negative pooled test statistic was set to zero, so fit will appear to be arbitrarily perfect. Robust corrections uninformative, not returned.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in lavaan.mi with a binary predictor
parts:
I get the following error:

"D3" only available using maximum likelihood estimation. Changed test to "D2".
If test = 'scaled.shifted' (estimator = 'WLSMV' or 'MLMV'), model comparison is only available by (re)setting test = 'D2' and pool.robust = TRUE.
Control more options by passing arguments to lavTestLRT() via the '...' argument.

None of these messages are errors, they just tell you what happened.  You can avoid seeing them if you set those arguments explicitly to override the default settings.  You only showed 1 model, but the message seems to indicate you are comparing models, is that right?
Negative pooled test statistic was set to zero, so fit will appear to be arbitrarily perfect. Robust corrections uninformative, not returned.

Negative pooled statistics can sometimes occur.  I do not know much about what conditions lead to them.  But I would hope that setting pool.robust = TRUE could avoid it.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

Okay, I will look to see if the warning should be tweaked for model comparison.
Should I change those settings in the sem.mi() function?

They are lavTestLRT() arguments, which you can also specify when calling fitMeasures().  Since you only called summary(fit, fit.m=TRUE), there is no way to pass those arguments.  You can just investigate fit in a separate call to fitMeasures().

messages.subject: Re: Error in lavaan.mi with a binary predictor
parts: I will look to see if the warning should be tweaked for model comparison.

Indeed, I had copied a check from lavTestLRT.mi() that did not belong in the fitMeasures() method because model comparison does not happen there. I removed the message about pool.robust=, and I wonder whether the same problem occurs when it is left FALSE.
Since you only called summary(fit, fit.m=TRUE), there is no way to pass those arguments

There is now.  I just added the ... argument to the summary() method to pass arguments to fitMeasures(), and subsequently to lavTestLRT.mi(), when fit.measures = TRUE.  You can install the development version:

https://github.com/simsem/semTools/wiki

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in lavaan.mi with a binary predictor
parts: I wasn't able to figure out how to pass those arguments via the summary() function

The ... argument just means you can use arguments of other functions that are called within summary(), or any generic function.  

summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE, pool.robust = TRUE, test = "D2")

The latter 2 arguments get passed to fitMeasures() inside summary(), when fit.measures = TRUE.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
